Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Burst profile data request for Dedicated sizing — Orbita integration

Hi Oliver —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. To get your Dedicated sizing estimate over the finish line we need a short burst/steady-state profile so our capacity team can map it to GPU SKUs and expected p99 latency under the target quantization profile. If you can fill the bullets below it will cut an extra day off our estimate.

Quick asks (feel free to paste values or attach a sample trace):
- Peak concurrent sessions during the 15-minute burst window (P95/P99 if available)
- Typical request mix: prompt tokens / expected response tokens (avg and 95th)
- Percent of requests that require streaming vs non-streaming output
- Session duration distribution (median and 99th) and whether you hold KV cache across requests
- Tolerance for graceful fallback (e.g., 100ms added p99 or fall back to smaller model)
- Any multi-model routing (reranker -> generator) or function/tool calls per request

Helpful but optional: a 1–2 hour token-level trace (CSV) or synthetic sample of 1k requests. I attached our redwood_preflight_template.xlsx — drop your numbers into the green sheet and I’ll run the estimator.

Timing: If we get this by EOD tomorrow we can surface a SKU-level proposal by Thursday.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0172

Attachments: redwood_preflight_template.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Oliver Park <oliver.park@orbita.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@orbita.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Burst profile data request for Dedicated sizing — Orbita integration

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks, quick answers inline and I attached a short token trace (sample_token_trace.csv) for your sizing team. I shaded what I'm less confident about.

- Peak concurrent sessions (15-min burst): 1,400 (P95 ~ 1,250; P99 ~ 1,380)
- Avg prompt tokens / avg response tokens: 120 / 420 (95th response tokens ~ 2,200)
- Streaming vs non-streaming: ~ 30% streaming (chat UI streaming partial tokens)
- Session duration: median 18s, P99 ~ 3m; we do keep KV cache for active sessions (reuse across rapid follow-ups)
- Fallback tolerance: prefer model fallback to smaller variant rather than added tail latency; p99 SLA target is 350ms for the primary generator model
- Multi-model routing: yes — light reranker stage (~0.03 calls per user request) followed by generator; occasional tool calls to our DB sync (0.01 calls/request)

Notes: The sample trace is from a product promo push last month — traffic shape is bursty for the first 30 minutes then decays. We can pull a longer trace if you need it.

Oliver
Oliver Park

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Oliver's quick answers and attached token trace. Highlights: 1.4k peak concurrent in a 15-min burst, avg response ~420 tokens, a 95th at ~2.2k tokens, streaming for 30% of requests, and they prefer model fallback over added p99 latency. P99 SLA target 350ms.

Ask: Can you run the estimator using the attached CSV and assume Quant-8 and Quant-4 candidate profiles, then produce:
- SKU-level capacity recommendation (min and recommended headroom for 99% day-one confidence)
- Expected p95/p99 latency for the chosen SKUs (generator + reranker path)
- Cost delta between Quant-8 and Quant-4 for sustained vs burst windows (per-token estimate)
- Risks/notes on KV cache retention and streaming tail impact

I put the HubSpot deal link here: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ORB-2028-1274 — let me know if you need more telemetry. Oliver, we might ping you for a 20-min call if the estimator needs clarifications.

Thanks — aiming to deliver the SKU proposal by Thursday COB.

Best,
Stephanie
